Hi team / James — attaching a first-pass package: redwood_ssq_answers_v1.xlsx and an annotated dataflow (redwood_dataflow_v1.png). Key points (summary):

- PII classification: We follow the customer's labeling but treat the following as PII by default when present in request payloads: names, email addresses, national identifiers, payment tokens, and health-related content flagged by the input schema. We list recommended pseudonymization per field in the SSQ workbook (see tab "Field Guidance").

- Storage and caches: For hosted API, we do not persist raw request payloads to long-term storage for generation requests by default. Short-lived KV cache (model-specific cache) may contain tokenized context in memory for up to 2 hours; if customer elects dedicated/private, cache persistence policies can be adjusted. For customers who require no persistent record, we offer a "no-retain" routing option for supported endpoints.

- Telemetry & monitoring: We collect anonymized usage telemetry for system health and model quality. Telemetry retention is configurable: default (90 days), reduced (30 days), and can be disabled for keying to a specific customer in Dedicated/Private deployments. Telemetry opt-out: for hosted customers, we can apply a per-account telemetry exclusion flag for PII-derived traces (requires an agreement on feature gating).

- KMS / key custody: Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS (Google KMS / AWS KMS depending on region) with key rotation; Dedicated/Private: customer-managed keys (BYOK) supported via KMS integrations and HSM-backed import. We can provide KMS attestation artifacts (SRK/KDF) upon NDA/procurement.

- Subprocessors: primary subprocessors that may handle request metadata or telemetry: AWS (EC2/EKS/S3), Google Cloud (BigQuery/logging where applicable), Datadog (monitoring only - redacted telemetry), S3-compatible backups provider. We include a full current roster in the SSQ workbook tab "Subprocessors" and will provide SOC2 attestations per vendor on request.

- Egress & controls: We use TLS 1.2+ in transit, strict egress firewall rules, and VPC peering options for Dedicated/Private. Dataflows in attached diagram mark egress paths and where pseudonymization/redaction hooks can be injected.

Attachments: redwood_ssq_answers_v1.xlsx, redwood_dataflow_v1.png

Kimberly: I flagged a few items in the SSQ that need security/legal confirmation (marked in yellow): KMS attestation language and the exact subprocessors for telemetry retention. Jonas: can you review the dataflow for any missing model-quality paths?

Hi James — thanks for the clarity. Please find the updated materials attached and notes inline below; attachments: redwood_dataflow_v2.png (egress-locked variant) and an updated workbook (redwood_ssq_answers_v1.xlsx updated). Also shared a Drive folder with the full evidence pack: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-surgitech-ssq.

Responses to your numbered items:

1) Telemetry/logging: Hosted mode does not persist full raw model inputs to long-term logs by default. Short-lived request traces used for debugging are stored in ephemeral tracing backends for up to 48 hours and are redacted to remove clearly identifiable PII fields unless the customer enables full request logging via an account option. Aggregated metrics used for monitoring (latency, token counts, error rates) are retained but do not contain raw text. We've added explicit language to the SSQ workbook (see tab "Logging & Telemetry").

2) KV cache: The runtime cache may hold tokenized context in memory; we do not write KV cache contents to disk in Hosted mode. For Dedicated/Private, cache persistence and encryption-at-rest are configurable; by default, on Dedicated we enable disk encryption for cache snapshots and support customer-managed KMS to protect snapshots. We've called this out in the workbook and diagram notes.

3) Datadog: Datadog receives only anonymized metrics and service-level traces with request identifiers — it does not receive raw payloads or stable hashes of content. We will provide the SOC2+Datadog control summary as an exhibit on request.

4) BYOK / HSM import: Private deployments support HSM-backed key import workflows; we integrate with common HSM providers via key import or external key references. There are two supported flows: (a) HSM import into a customer-managed cloud KMS, or (b) customer HSM with a connector where keys never leave the HSM and Redwood holds only references. Limitations: on-prem HSM connectors require network allowlist and direct peering; we'll include the architecture note in the Drive folder.
